races.name: John Bircham And Stephen "Jagger" Hayes Memorial Juvenile Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)
Happy 80th Birthday Ted Hull Mares' Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Arfursgal
runners_data.note: Consistent form profile with two places from four runs on Good ground and a lightly-raced 5yo profile for Honeyball; unknown natural style (U-tagged) but the Good-ground placing record and 54-day break suggest she arrives fresh and capable of getting competitive in the straight.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a modest strike-rate (0W from 15 Good-ground runs) and a 10lb claimer aboard; the 7yo's recent form shows flashes of placing ability but this trip and track may stretch his resolution at the finish.

runners_data.name: Diamond White
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the ride for an O'Neill yard in decent 14-day form; has two second-place finishes on Good and holds a legitimate claim on the prominent slots, with her best effort coming over this sort of distance and conditions.

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton teams up with Dan Skelton (6 wins from 21 over 14 days) on a mare who has already won on Good going over 16f — the best recent form-line in the field and the most obvious beneficiary if she can slot into second or third from Steal A Glance's lead.

runners_data.name: Crystal Jet
runners_data.note: Toby Bulgin's 4yo has a win on Good at 16f and compact form figures of 331; by nature a prominent racer, she is unlikely to secure that berth today given the congestion forward and the STYLE_FIT tag should temper expectations of a forward-pressing performance.

runners_data.name: Lundy View
runners_data.note: Three runs all resulting in 6th or 7th on Good, all over 17f for Nigel Hawke — a yard with no runners in the past 14 days; the consistent finishes in the rear half suggest this mare needs significantly more than competitors ahead are offering before she figures.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Honeyball's 4yo is the race's one true front-runner; the 5lb claim on Bament may blunt the advantage slightly, but uncontested access to the lead on Good at Newton Abbot is a genuine tactical asset — STYLE_FIT tag notes she has been placed out of role before, but here the lead is entirely available.

runners_data.name: Take The Boat
runners_data.note: Bannister rides a mare with an honest 23 form-line for Georgina Nicholls; genuinely prominent by instinct but unlikely to fulfil that role given the prominent logjam — racing behind her natural position, her three Good-ground places came in less competitive fields and the STYLE_FIT discount applies here.

races.paceDynamic: Steal A Glance is the lone confirmed front-runner and, ridden by the 5lb claimer Chad Bament, is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested clip through Newton Abbot's tight turns, setting a sustainable gallop that rewards those who can travel close to the pace rather than those who need a truly searching test. Crystal Jet and Take The Boat are both natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred berth, so expect some positional friction in the early exchanges as Getmyfriend and Diamond White — genuine prominent types with legitimate claims on second and third rank — press forward alongside Steal A Glance. This field holds more front-running and prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate; Steal A Glance is best-placed to lead, with Getmyfriend and Diamond White most likely to actually secure the prominent positions ahead of the redistributed Crystal Jet and Take The Boat. A single uncontested leader on Good ground over a strongly-run 2m1f hurdle course historically favours established prominent racers who travel fluently and quicken at the business end — this race shape strongly suits the prominent-to-pace profile, particularly horses who have already shown they can win or place racing forward.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steal A Glance Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Steal A Glance crosses cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead with Getmyfriend and Diamond White in tow.
scenarios.body: Steal A Glance sets a controlled fractions-friendly pace that turns the race into a test of jumping fluency and a sharp finish rather than stamina, rewarding those sitting just behind with cover and energy in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrap Quickens Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If early positional rivalry between Crystal Jet, Take The Boat and the front group lifts the pace and turns this into a more genuine test.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early gallop stretches the field and exposes hold-up horses who are not truly built for that role, with the race cracking open from the top of the home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and a fresher hold-up horse swoops from behind.
scenarios.body: Arfursgal, with consistent form at this level and similar-ground placing, is best-positioned of the closers to exploit a drop in tempo, though true hold-up types are scarce and this scenario relies on the prominent pack tying each other up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Fallers Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers or traffic incidents reshuffle the field and render early position irrelevant.
scenarios.body: Newton Abbot's tight, unforgiving circuit can generate interference at hurdles that negates a prominent position and hands an advantage to horses who have found daylight on the outside, though this remains the least-likely outcome in a small, eight-runner field.

watchPoints.text: Steal A Glance's ability to dictate terms unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if she is allowed to coast at her own fractions, the prominent brigade behind her will be racing in the optimum position; watch whether Bament controls or capitulates at the first bend.

Crystal Jet and Take The Boat are both natural prominent types who cannot both get there — early jostling between them and Getmyfround/Diamond White on Newton Abbot's sharp opening furlong could create a bump or interference that scrambles the intended race order.

Getmyfriend arrives with the most convincing form in the field (a win on Good at 16f plus a Dan Skelton/Harry Skelton combination in good recent form) — if she travels fluently behind the leader her finishing kick becomes the race's primary threat.

Ask Peter has 15 runs on Good ground without a win, and James Robottom (10lb claimer) is riding for the same yard as Arfursgal and Diamond White — watch for any stable-level preference or riding orders that might affect how aggressively he is deployed.

Lundy View's three runs have all produced rear-division finishes on identical going and trip — she is one to leave out of most scenarios, but a scrappy, interference-ridden race could accidentally bring a previously unconsidered runner into play from the back.

races.name: Dick Oliver At Newton Abbot Races Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls in excellent 14-day form (1/1), returned just 6 days ago suggesting race fitness is high; holds up naturally but can race handy, and the Good ground suits based on a win and two placings from seven similar-going runs — the 2m5f trip is within his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: It's A Breeze won last time out and quickly backs that up just six days later, already having today's trip and going under his belt. The form before that win was patchier though, including a pulled-up run and a fall, the obvious reservation.

runners_data.name: The Gypsy Davey
runners_data.note: Strong recent Good-ground record (14 runs, 2 wins, 5 places) and Conor Ring has a live booking here; a natural hold-up type who has placed at this sort of trip on Good going before, though the headgear change to visor last time out is worth monitoring for consistency.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and fresh from a run just six days ago, The Gypsy Davey tops our figures in this field despite an official rating of only 97. He's yet to win in his last five starts, though, including a pulled-up effort in that sequence, the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Chief Black Robe
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien sends this 10-year-old out after a 71-day break, which demands attention for fitness; he is a true hold-up horse placed into the midfield picture only by the volume of closers in this field, meaning he races at the back — his best chance depends on a stronger pace than Senor Diaz is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Chief Black Robe was second five starts back, and third two starts back, form that puts him third in our figures despite being yet to win in his last five starts. A 71-day absence since a modest sixth last time out, following two untidy efforts in between, is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's six-year-old is lightly exposed over fences and showed a placed effort 22 days ago; by nature he wants to come from well off the pace, but with so many hold-up types competing for the same ground his actual position in running will be deep, making a winning run structurally difficult against this pace map.
runners_data.comment: Chillhi is our selection, with our figures rating him well above his official mark of 88. He was third three starts back and returns quickly, just 19 days after pulling up last time out, with today's trip and going already banked, though that mixed form remains the reservation.

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: The form string contains a recent win (1 in PP1P-4 sequence) but that win came on Soft ground; Robbie Llewellyn's 9-year-old has only 3 placings from 8 similar-going runs and 0 wins on Good, so the surface is a genuine question mark here — he is a hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by field composition.
runners_data.comment: Flashy Boy won three starts back but has pulled up in three of his last five starts, a stop-start profile. He already has today's trip and going under his belt, though a 58-day absence leaves questions, and our figures rate him only on a par with his official mark of 77.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Nigel Hawke's 8-year-old has been placed three times on similar ground but has never won on Good, and 42 days since last run plus the lowest OR in the field at 72 makes it hard to construct a winning scenario; placed to race from further back than natural, finishing speed on a slow pace is limited.
runners_data.comment: Watchoutitscookie blows hot and cold, with a third three starts back, and a third five starts back, split by a seventh, leaving him seventh of eight in our figures. He already has today's trip and going banked, but a 42-day break adds to the case against him.

runners_data.name: Senor Diaz
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in this field and the key pace-setter; Jimmy Frost's 7-year-old ran third 53 days ago and gets an uncontested lead, which is the most significant tactical advantage in this race — the question is whether his jumping under pressure over 2m5f is reliable enough to sustain the advantage.
runners_data.comment: Senor Diaz was third last time out, an improvement on a mixed sequence that included three pulled-up runs. Our figures rate him well above his official mark of 69, with today's trip and going already banked, but a 53-day absence and that mixed form keep him just a midfield player.

runners_data.name: Emberscombe
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle is in good 14-day form (2/7) and this 9-year-old has winning form — including a recent course-relevant effort — but his natural inclination to come from off the pace leaves him needing more gallop than Senor Diaz's controlled lead is likely to generate; the 18-day turnaround is no concern for fitness.
runners_data.comment: Emberscombe won three starts back, and won five starts back too, form that sits oddly with her bottom-of-the-field rating here. She already has today's trip and going under her belt and returns quickly, 18 days on, but a modest sixth last time out leaves her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Senor Diaz is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, James Best can dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front over the 2m5f trip on Good turf at Newton Abbot. That lone-leader scenario creates a sustainable, rhythmic pace that will not test the stragglers early but will compress the field into a procession, leaving precious little room for hold-up horses to generate momentum off a strong pace. The race shape heavily favours Senor Diaz himself to control the tempo, and behind him the prominent-to-midfield runners — It's A Breeze and The Gypsy Davey — who can travel handily without being too far back to challenge. The field holds considerably more true hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Chief Black Robe, Chillhi, Flashy Boy, Watchoutitscookie and Emberscombe are all genuine hold-up horses, with only the most forward-thinking of them likely to secure a closer tracking position; the remainder will be racing further back than ideal. The clear tactical verdict is that patient hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged here — a lone leader over a stiff staying trip on Good ground favours those who can track just off the pace and pounce from a handy position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Senor Diaz Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Diaz sets an uncontested lead and is never seriously headed, converting front-running control into a genuine winning chance.
scenarios.body: Senor Diaz dictates a comfortable pace through the early fences, builds his stamina advantage over 2m5f, and the Good ground suits his relaxed travelling style; no hold-up horse generates enough momentum from off a slow pace to reel him in up the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Diaz weakens at the final fence and a handy tracker swoops from just off the pace to win.
scenarios.body: It's A Breeze or The Gypsy Davey, both settled handy and comfortable on Good ground, inherit the lead as Senor Diaz's jumping effort tells late; their hold-up tendency relative to the true front-runner still gives them enough cover to travel efficiently and sprint clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and creates enough tempo for one of the redistributed closers to finish powerfully from the rear.
scenarios.body: Chief Black Robe, most experienced in this field at 10 years old with solid Good-ground credentials, or Emberscombe, whose recent course form is relevant, manages to find a clear run and close down a tiring leader; this scenario is discounted because the likely slow pace handicaps true hold-up types structurally.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart — Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or unseats reduce the race to a contest of survival rather than speed, with a low-rated stayer scrambling home.
scenarios.body: Chillhi or Watchoutitscookie, both capable of staying the trip and benefiting from a depleted field, inherit a position they could never achieve on merit; this is a low-probability chaos scenario relying entirely on misfortune for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Senor Diaz's jumping accuracy is the single biggest swing factor — any mistake at a fence could immediately promote a tracker into a winning position and unravel the dominant Scenario A entirely.

With five natural hold-up horses compressed into a midfield cluster, traffic and interference in the closing stages is a real risk — watch for Chillhi, Chief Black Robe and Watchoutitscookie getting hampered if the pace bunches the field together.
It's A Breeze returns just six days after its last run — monitor paddock behaviour and early jumping for any signs of fatigue or a below-par physical state, given the short turnaround.

Chief Black Robe (71 days since last run) and Flashy Boy (58 days) are both returning from extended breaks — fitness-related errors at fences over 2m5f on Good ground should be anticipated, particularly at the later obstacles.

The Good going is consistent across all races at Newton Abbot today with no deterioration reported — no horse faces an unexpected surface concern, but Flashy Boy's record specifically on Good (0 wins from 3 runs) is worth keeping in mind when assessing its chances.

races.name: Brendon Soper Memorial Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Son Of Hypnos
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up performer who handles Good ground well (a win and a place in similar conditions), but his recent form — 7th twice from 16f and 19f trips — suggests he's not hitting top form; a tongue strap is fitted and the 7lb claimer Jack Stenhouse takes a significant chunk of weight off, which is the main positive angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, but a third three starts back is the pick of that sequence, and he rates clear of this field on our figures. Has run over today's trip and going before, though a pulled-up effort and 38 days off add caution.

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago which warrants scrutiny on freshness grounds, though Joe Tizzard's yard have had three runners in 14 days including this horse; a genuine hold-up type whose Good-ground record (two placed efforts from nine runs) is acceptable but unspectacular, and the 2m2½f trip is longer than his most recent runs at 2m1f.

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: A 10lb claimer in Osian Radford takes the ride, and trainer Mrs C Williams has had six runners in 14 days with one winner — a yard firing; Linden Lane is a consistent hold-up performer who has placed four times in recent starts and handles Good ground, making him a solid each-way profile if the pace scenario opens up.
runners_data.comment: Two thirds in his last five starts underline solid, consistent form, and he ranks second of eight on our figures as the chief threat here. He remains winless in that sequence, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer with a 15-from-15 record on similar going, and he showed a placed effort last time out; his natural style is to race from the rear but with so many hold-up types in this field, he is unlikely to get the truly strongly-run race he needs to deliver his best — the style-fit discount is real and tempers his chance.
runners_data.comment: A third three starts back is the standout line in a mixed sequence, and a quick seven-day turnaround keeps him fresh enough to feature as a threat on our figures. He remains winless in that run, with a fall among the finishes too.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and key pace-setter; two wins from his last four starts including a 20f victory on Good ground, and the tongue strap and cheekpieces suggest trainer Barry John Murphy has him set up to perform — the probability of this horse controlling the race entirely is high.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts, including last time out, show he's capable on his day, but a ninth and a fifth in that spell reveal inconsistency. Has run over today's trip and going before, and sits fifth of eight on our figures.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Won at 18f on Good just six days ago (quick turnaround noted), and cheekpieces are fitted again; a genuine prominent racer who should lock onto Makinbecon's heels from an early stage, making him the most natural beneficiary if the leader stops — trainer Joe Tickle has been in excellent form with two winners from seven in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: He has plenty to find against this field, ranked seventh of eight on our figures, though a placed effort last time out and a win two starts back show some remaining ability. Quick to reappear just six days on, having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: A hold-up type by inclination who tends to race prominently when headgear is applied (cheekpieces today), but in this field his natural rear position has been compressed toward midfield — handles Good ground well with three placed efforts, though his finishing kick from that position is uncertain against better-placed rivals.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and again four starts back, he can be relied on for a bold showing, though a ninth and a fifth in between make him frustratingly inconsistent. He remains winless in his last five starts, with 26 days since that effort.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 77, a five-year-old still learning the game; naturally a back-of-the-field type but squeezed into midfield by the volume of hold-up horses here, and Good ground is familiar territory across his entire career record — needs significant improvement on a 6th and two 5ths in recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out heads a modest sequence, and quick to reappear just seven days on, she rates well above her official mark as a leading threat here. She remains winless in her last five starts, with two sixths and a ninth also featuring.

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come over 16f and this 2m2½f trip is a clear step up in distance — whether that stamina question is answered positively is the central query; normally a hold-up type running without the benefit of a strongly-run race today given the race shape, and Nick Scholfield's yard has been active with two winners from nine in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: A mixed sequence including a pulled-up run and a ninth make him hard to fancy, and he sits bottom of our figures in this field. A second four starts back is the one bright spot, though 32 days off and a winless run of late count against him.

races.paceDynamic: Makinbecon is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him from the front, he should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m2½f trip on Good turf at Newton Abbot. Saucats is the only other prominent-leaning runner and will likely slot in behind Makinbecon, meaning the pace is set by one horse with minimal external pressure — a recipe for a steady early tempo that doesn't string the field out. This race shape, with a lone leader dictating from the front and a relatively bunched mid-pack of hold-up types, heavily favours the prominent and front-running profiles, as a controlled gallop denies the hold-up horses the strongly-run race they need to produce a late burst. It is also worth noting that this field contains far more genuine hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Applejack Poet, Man Oh Man, Yanka Blue, and Mi Sueno are all true back-of-the-field types who have been mapped to midfield simply to reflect the race's physical shape, but in reality they will likely be racing in a compressed group behind the leaders, unable to secure their ideal ground-making position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Makinbecon Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Makinbecon is allowed to dictate a steady, uncontested gallop from the front and no rival mounts early pressure.
scenarios.body: Makinbecon sets his own fractions, conserves energy jumping hurdles cleanly, and simply outstays rivals who can't produce a meaningful late challenge from a compressed hold-up pack; Saucats, tracking closely throughout, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotts Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Saucats or another prominent type pushes Makinbecon into a genuine contest from the second circuit, raising the early tempo.
scenarios.body: A faster gallop stretches the field and punishes any runner carrying extra weight or lacking the jumping fluency to maintain position; hold-up horses who can survive the quickening tempo into the straight have their best chance here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and the hold-up pack sweeps past a tiring Makinbecon in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: True hold-up types like Son Of Hypnos or Ugo Bingo can theoretically produce a late flourish, though their redistribution to midfield means they are less likely to find clear daylight at a crucial moment; this scenario is discounted because many so-called closers here are not racing from their natural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Errors And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or interference disrupt the race shape entirely, scrambling positional plans across the field.
scenarios.body: A reduced or fractured field with gaps in the running changes who benefits, potentially allowing a hold-up horse to find a clear run it would otherwise never have secured; lower-rated runners like Yanka Blue or Mi Sueno could creep into contention if market leaders are eliminated.

watchPoints.text: Makinbecon is the fulcrum of this race — if he jumps cleanly and bowls along unchallenged, the entire field is racing to his tune; watch for any jumping error at an early hurdle that would disrupt his rhythm and potentially trigger Scenario D.

Saucats runs for the second time in six days and any sign of dullness or sluggishness in the early stages would remove the only horse capable of pressuring Makinbecon — monitor his pre-race demeanour and how sharply he breaks.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Applejack Poet, Man Oh Man, Yanka Blue, Mi Sueno — will likely bunch in a compressed midfield group; watch for traffic problems and interference turning for home if the pace suddenly quickens.

Mi Sueno steps up markedly in trip from 16f to 2m2½f today — if he finds the extra distance, his finishing effort could be more potent than his recent form suggests, but it is a genuine unknown and worth monitoring early to see if he travels comfortably.

Linden Lane's 10lb claimer Osian Radford is worth tracking — a 10lb weight pull is significant in a handicap hurdle, and if the young conditional rider settles him well off the pace through the early stages, the horse's consistent placed record makes him a runner to keep onside throughout.

races.name: Zero To Exit Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Byzantium
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner trained by Paul Nicholls (1/1 T14) with solid good-ground form (9/12 sim-going, 2W2P) and the confidence of a recent course win at 22f; at 6 years old and 53 days off a run, freshness is likely on her side, though the step to 3m2½f is a slight stamina query and her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she would be vulnerable if asked to race out of her natural lead role.
runners_data.comment: Byzantium won five starts back and is second-rated in our figures carrying 170 lb, with experience of this going already banked. The concern is only fifth last time out and a refusal earlier in the sequence, following a 53-day break.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with exceptional good-ground credentials (7W10P in similar going over 24-26f trips), who showed a third recently over C&D-ish distances and carries cheekpieces — Bryan Carver takes the ride for Chris Honour who has no recent runners (T14:0/0), so the booking of an experienced amateur is worth noting; he is a prominent type who should sit ideally placed tracking Byzantium.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, and a winner three starts back, Time To Bite has flanked that success with places either side and returns quickly, 21 days on. He already has today's trip and going under his belt and tops our figures, the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 7-year-old in excellent form (1-2-2-1 in last four completed), arriving just 6 days after a run which requires monitoring, though Harry Skelton's judgment with Dan Skelton horses (6/21 T14) is usually sound; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to be honest enough to allow a sustained late run over this stamina-testing trip.

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Consistent staying type (1W5P in sim-going) with a clear preference for good ground and distances around 25-26f, handled by a 5lb claimer in Fern O'Brien which could prove significant in a finish; a natural hold-up runner who will need the leaders to tire but whose record of placing without winning suggests he may fill a frame slot rather than land the prize.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, and a winner four starts back, Jager Time has been freely consistent without threatening the principals, and sits fifth of six in our figures. He does already have today's trip and going under his belt, his best point on paper.

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a solid placing profile (1W8P in sim-going over staying trips), trained by Anthony Honeyball whose T14 of 2/2 is a positive flag; the switch back to good ground after a soft-ground run suits, and at OR 100 he may get into this off a lenient mark if Time To Bite or Byzantium weaken.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, Juggernaut has still been admirably consistent with two seconds and two thirds among them, and sits third in our figures with today's trip and going both banked. The 56-day absence since his latest run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with multiple second and third placings (1W6P), but his true style is a hold-up rear-of-field runner — he has been placed in midfield on the map simply because there are more hold-up types than rear slots available, and securing his natural position in a small field where the pace is modest may prove difficult; Callum Pritchard takes over for Barry John Murphy (1/10 T14) and the 9-year-old's record suggests he finds winning elusive.
runners_data.comment: I Am Spider Man was in the frame in each of his four previous starts before a seventh last time out. He sits fourth in our figures, already has today's trip and going banked, and returns quickly after just 14 days - that flat last run the query.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: A 6-year-old with no wins or places from 5 sim-going runs (0W0P) and an alarming form string including two non-completions (U, F), who carries the heaviest weight concession off OR 85; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up style because rear slots are oversubscribed, and Tabitha Worsley's amateur claim cannot disguise that Harriet Dickin's T14 reads 0/2 — the most vulnerable runner in the field on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Stavanger Rose is bottom of our figures, with a fall and an unseated rider among her last five starts leaving little to work with. She does already have experience of today's going and is fit having run 18 days ago, but the profile makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Byzantium is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to take her on for the lead over 3m2½f on good ground at Newton Abbot, she should be able to dictate at a controlled, energy-conserving tempo from the front. Time To Bite and Juggernaut will likely press forward to dispute a prominent berth behind her, giving the race a small lead group and a bunched chasing pack rather than a strung-out procession. The hold-up horses — Muskerry Rock and Jager Time — will have to be patient off what may prove a deceptively steady early gallop, meaning they face the challenge of a late injection of pace rather than grinding relentlessness. I Am Spider Man and Stavanger Rose are genuine rear-of-field types who have been mapped to midfield because the field contains more hold-up horses than can all sit at the back; in practice they may be unable to get the wide, daylight-seeking position they need, which compromises their natural game. This race shape strongly favours a prominent, well-placed runner who can track Byzantium at low cost and produce a sustained challenge from the second-last, rather than a big-finishing closer who needs the pace to be honest throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Byzantium Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Byzantium is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a steady but true enough gallop that denies closers a clean swoop.
scenarios.body: Byzantium uses her natural front-running ability to dictate the fractions, keeping the field organised behind her and saving enough for the long Newton Abbot run-in; at 3m2½f on good ground her stamina profile gives her every chance of lasting home. The prominent horses Time To Bite and Juggernaut, who sit closest in tracking positions, are best placed to pounce if Byzantium weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Byzantium's pace proves just slow enough to leave her vulnerable to a well-timed challenge from a prominent tracker in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Time To Bite, with strong good-ground form over this sort of trip (7W10P in similar going) and experience at the highest end of this field, is ideally positioned to pounce if Byzantium's race-long exertion tells after the last; Juggernaut's consistent placing record and handler Anthony Honeyball's strong T14 record supports a bold show. Both horses suit a tactical race that comes alive in the final mile rather than a true test of stamina from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely honest from the front and the lead group weaken, allowing the genuine hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Muskerry Rock and Jager Time both carry strong recent form over comparable distances on good ground and have the stamina profiles to benefit from a grinding test; Muskerry Rock in particular has won at 26f in good conditions and Harry Skelton's positive partnership with his brother's yard is a notable angle. However, this scenario is only partly likely because the early pace is unlikely to be truly punishing with Byzantium in control, limiting the closing opportunity.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, a fall, or interference early scrambles positions and creates a messy, stop-start race that nullifies the front-runner's advantage.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic scenario redistributed hold-up horses I Am Spider Man and Stavanger Rose might accidentally gain the prominent position they could not achieve tactically, though their [STYLE_FIT] and redistribution flags underline that this would be circumstantial rather than natural. Stavanger Rose's erratic form (UF in recent history) and I Am Spider Man's tendency to finish in minor placings rather than win means neither is likely to capitalise fully even in a muddled race.

watchPoints.text: Byzantium's early pace control is the linchpin of the entire race shape — if she is pressured unexpectedly by Time To Bite or Juggernaut jumping boldly, the race could unravel quickly and genuine closers like Muskerry Rock would be handed a winning opportunity.

Muskerry Rock runs just 6 days after her last outing, and while Dan Skelton routinely targets horses on quick turnarounds, any sign of residual fatigue in the paddock or early jumping should be noted — she needs to be travelling well into the home straight or her chance evaporates.

I Am Spider Man and Stavanger Rose will struggle to find their natural wide, hold-up position in a field of only 7 runners where Byzantium controls the pace — watch whether their jockeys are forced to switch tactics and race more prominently than suits either horse.

Time To Bite's age (11) and the weight of 169lbs over 3m2½f on good ground deserves monitoring in the closing stages — his good-ground form is excellent but his finishing effort late in a stamina test at this age could fade if Byzantium has not gone quite fast enough to soften the rivals ahead of him.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist on Good ground with a solid 3/3 sim-going profile, trained by Nick Scholfield alongside Edgewell — returns after 30 days, has not yet won over a trip this long, and Jack Quinlan's claiming allowance is not available here; must produce a late challenge from the rear and the pace scenario may not stretch the field enough.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back, and another four starts back, mark him a leading danger, backed up by a second two starts back before that. He dips to a below-par fifth last time out but has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: No More No
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: four wins on Good ground including three times over 3m, returns after 40 days with Brendan Powell aboard and has clearly thrived fresh before; wearing hood and tongue-tie, she sets the pace entirely on her own terms and her 4W record in sim-going is the standout stat in the race.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last four starts, interrupted only by a seventh three starts back, mark him a big threat on pure form, despite a rating below his official mark. He has run over today's distance and going before, though 40 days off is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Great d'Ange
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up type with 14 runs on sim-going and only one win to show, ridden by a 3lb claimer Tom Broughton who reduces the 162lb burden usefully; ran 16 days ago and has placed at 3m+ before, but the PP (pulled up twice) in recent form raises stamina/jumping reliability concerns.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort last time out marks a big step forward, and he sits narrowly ahead of this field on our figures as the one to beat. Two pulled-up efforts further back are the one blot, but he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of a win nine days ago — the shortest LR gap in this field — and holds four wins over comparable distances on Good ground; his natural style is to come from the rear, but the congested hold-up group means he is unlikely to get the clean passage he needs and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations in this shape.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: Returning from a 323-day absence for Grace Harris, who has sent out two winners from 13 runners in the last fortnight; her last three sim-going runs include two wins and a second over comparable trips, and her prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking No More No — the layoff is the primary concern.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts, either side of a runner-up effort, show she has real ability on her day, but that form is 323 days old and the long layoff is the major concern. She has, at least, run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield map position she is unlikely to occupy naturally; her recent form includes two seconds on Good ground over similar trips, but at 10 years old and 148lbs she has not won in 10 sim-going starts and Conor Ring will need a gap to appear at exactly the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and again four starts back, with a third two starts back in between, mark her a leading danger on consistent form. Winless in that spell but rated above her official mark on our figures, she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer at this trip but a true sit-and-wait type mapped to midfield due to field congestion — has two career wins and a recent fifth after a break, which is modest; the combination of redistribution, STYLE_FIT discount, and soft-ground wins in history makes him a harder case to make in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-up runs mid-sequence make him hard to trust, though a runner-up effort five starts back shows some ability when things click. He remains winless in his last five starts and rates sixth of seven, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Testflight
runners_data.note: Placed in five of her last five over 3m+ trips on Good and similar ground, making her a reliable each-way option at big prices; the consistent 3-4 finishes suggest she will run her race without threatening front-runners in a moderate-pace scenario, but Sue Gardner's 0/3 14-day record and Tabitha Worsley's amateur status are small negatives.
runners_data.comment: Three thirds and two fourths in his last five starts show admirable consistency without ever threatening to win, leaving him bottom of our figures here. He remains winless in that run, but has run over today's distance and going before.

races.paceDynamic: No More No is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse willing to lead, will dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 3m2f on Good ground — nobody is likely to press or challenge for the early lead, meaning the pace will be honest rather than punishing. My Girl Katie and Testflight are the other prominent types who may attempt to race close behind but neither has the credentials to force a genuine test, so the pace picture is essentially settled from the outset. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Edgewell, Honey I'm Good, and Mcgregors Charge are all genuine hold-up horses reshuffled into midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally, meaning the bunch in the middle of the field will be larger and more congested than the map implies. This race shape — a moderate, uncontested gallop set by a single front-runner — strongly favours horses able to travel close to the pace without expending energy, then pick off a potentially tired leader in the final mile; the prominent-to-midfield profile benefits most, while true closers face a harder task if the tempo never truly stretches the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If No More No dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the pack stalks without incident before closing on the home turn.
scenarios.body: No More No sets fractions entirely to suit herself and arrives at the final fences full of running, but horses who have tracked economically within a couple of lengths will have enough left to collar her; the prominent-to-midfield trackers who travel smoothly get first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If No More No's controlled gallop is so well-judged that she maintains enough in reserve to repel all challengers up the straight.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to apply early pressure, No More No builds an insuperable lead into the home straight and her rivals — having sat in a pack — find it hard to close the gap quickly over the final fences; this shape rewards exactly the type of controlled front-running she has demonstrated four times in Good-ground races.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Get Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely moderate enough to compress the field and the hold-up horses find clear daylight to finish through.
scenarios.body: Edgewell and Premier Fantasy, who carry strong recent Good-ground form and proven finishing ability, pick their way through from an honest midfield position in the final half-mile; however, the redistribution of multiple true hold-up types into the middle of the race means traffic and congestion are real risks that reduce the probability of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or attrition at fences remove key rivals early, reshaping the contest entirely.
scenarios.body: A field with several 10-year-olds and horses carrying higher weights over a long 3m2f trip on Good ground creates genuine risk of non-completions; the horse who survives and jumps cleanest, regardless of style, inherits a race by default.

watchPoints.text: No More No is uncontested in front over 3m2f on Good ground — if she builds a lead of more than 5 lengths at halfway, the hold-up types running out of their natural position will struggle to close efficiently.

My Girl Katie returns from 323 days off; if she travels badly or makes jumping errors early, the prominent race-shape loses its primary challenger to No More No and the scenario calculus shifts sharply toward the front-runner.
Edgewell runs for the second time in nine days — monitor closely for any sign of fatigue or a laboured jump at the early fences, as a tired jump can cascade into a fall or refusal over a 3m2f trip.

Traffic congestion is a structural risk: Edgewell, Honey I'm Good, and Mcgregors Charge are all natural hold-up horses forced into the midfield pack — watch for crowding on the final bend that could cost any of them a winning run.

Great d'Ange has pulled up twice in recent form; if the 10-year-old shows any sign of jumping hesitantly or losing interest before the final circuit, take note as it may signal an early withdrawal from contention.
